चेदि — N. of a country and their people. The Cedis were also called Ḍāhalas and Traipuras; they occupied the banks of the Narmadā and were the same as the people of दशार्ण q. v. Their capital was at one time त्रिपुरी q. v. The Cedis are considered by some to have inhabited the modern Bundelkhand in Central India, while by others their country is identified with the modern Chandail. The Haihayas or Kalacuris ruled at Māhiṣmatī situated on the Narmadā between the Vindhya and Ṛkṣa mountains about Bheraghar below Jabbalpur.
